collection.description: A child wonders why the daylight sky looks blue.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (child) wonders why the daylight sky looks blue.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: (scholar), a researcher, explains that sunlight scatters through air and blue light scatters strongly.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: (child) compares the sky at noon and sunset.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: (adult) jokes that the sea painted the sky, then identifies it as pretend.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: (child) invents a colorful story and asks for the real explanation afterward.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: (adult), a naturalist, points out how clouds, air, and sunlight change the view.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: (child) notices that the sky looks different after rain.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: (adult) and (child) compare shadows and colors over several days.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: (adult) seeks help from (scholar), a researcher, rather than guessing.
